skill: Nonlinear Equations In One Variable And Systems Of Equations In Two Variables
prompt:
$$x - b = (x - b)(x - 18)$$

Which of the following are solutions to the given equation, where $b$ is a constant and $b > 19$?

I. $b$
II. $18$
III. $19$
explanation: Choice B is correct. Subtracting the expression $(x - b)$ from both sides of the given equation yields $0 = (x - b)(x - 18) - (x - b)$, which can be rewritten as $0 = (x - b)(x - 18) + (-1)(x - b)$. Since the two terms on the right-hand side of this equation have a common factor of $(x - b)$, it can be rewritten as $0 = (x - b)(x - 18 + (-1))$, or $0 = (x - b)(x - 19)$. By the zero product property, it follows that $x - b = 0$ or $x - 19 = 0$. Adding $b$ to both sides of the equation $x - b = 0$ yields $x = b$. Adding $19$ to both sides of the equation $x - 19 = 0$ yields $x = 19$. Therefore, the two solutions to the given equation are $b$ and $19$. Thus, only $b$ and $19$, not $18$, are solutions to the given equation.
